[open] Issue #785: TestNewVRAMLimiterContextCancelReleasesBlocked is flaky on loaded CI runners
  Author: @anchapin
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/issues/785

  Description:
    ### What
    `TestNewVRAMLimiterContextCancelReleasesBlocked` in `internal/concurrencylimit/limiter_test.go` is unreliable on loaded CI runners. The test uses `time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)` to wait for a waiter goroutine to park in `cond.Wait()` before calling `cancel()`. On idle or lightly-loaded runners this is usually sufficient, but on saturated CI runners the scheduler may not have parked the waiter before `cancel()` fires, causing `context.Canceled` to be returned instead of `context.DeadlineExceeded`.
    
    ### Why
    This test causes spurious CI failures that are not indicative of any real bug — they are a test-implementation artifact. The current workaround (accepting both `Canceled` and `DeadlineExceeded` + 500 ms sleep) is a band-aid, not a proper fix. The sleep-based synchronization is inherently non-deterministic.
    
    ### Acceptance Criteria
    - [ ] Replace `time.Sleep` with a reliable synchronization mechanism (e.g., a `sync.WaitGroup` + a `ready chan struct{}`) so the test reliably waits for the waiter to actually enter `cond.Wait()` before `cancel()` fires
    - [ ] After refactoring, remove the `|| errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` branch from the assertion, keeping only `context.DeadlineExceeded`
    - [ ] `make test-race` passes ≥10 consecutive runs under moderate load (e.g., `stress` tool or repeated `go test -race -count=10`)
    - [ ] The refactored test documents *why* `DeadlineExceeded` is the expected error (explicit `cancel()` call vs. timeout expiry) so future readers understand the semantics
    
    ### Technical Notes
    - The test sits in `internal/concurrencylimit/limiter_test.go` at `TestNewVRAMLimiterContextCancelReleasesBlocked`
    - A proper fix uses a \"ready\" channel: the waiter closes `ready` after entering `cond.Wait()`, the test reads `ready` before calling `cancel()`
    - Do NOT simply increase the sleep further — that papers over the race without fixing it
